core_claim: Ali Wong's Baby Cobra is a two-act, six-levels-deep architectural construction, and its biggest laughs depend on lines delivered 12 to 46 minutes earlier.

edt_01.label: Hook — A laugh 46 minutes in the making
edt_01.title: A laugh 46 minutes in the making
edt_01.editorial_notes: Open with the concrete scene — minute 50:57, a miscarriage joke that calls back to minute 4:46. Do not round the 46-minute gap. Keep Wong's mother-quote exact.

edt_02.label: Two acts, not ten topics
edt_02.title: Two acts, not ten topics
edt_02.editorial_notes: The '85% of runtime is marriage + pregnancy' claim must be exact. The six-levels-of-nesting finding is the core visual anchor.

edt_03.label: The audience laughs from minute two on
edt_03.title: The shape of an hour of laughter
edt_03.editorial_notes: Timeline chart is the centerpiece of this section. Annotate minute 11 (peak 1) and minute 49/50 (peak 2).

edt_04.label: Turn — the second peak reveals structure
edt_04.title: The second peak
edt_04.editorial_notes: Narrative pivot of the whole piece. Explicitly pair each callback (hippies, mom, wet) with its source line — quotes must be verbatim. The 38.1 laugh-s/min conception bit number is load-bearing. This section should include the interactive callback-arc visualization.

edt_05.label: A callback is not magic — 1.34x
edt_05.title: A callback is a runway
edt_05.editorial_notes: 1.34x multiplier is the honest, non-mystifying number. Keep it explicit. The 'runway/plane' metaphor is editorial.

edt_06.label: Most of the hour is setup
edt_06.title: 61.9% of the hour is silent
edt_06.editorial_notes: Setup-to-payoff ratio frame. The nesting-depth-vs-duration chart ties the 'shrinking bits' point to data.

edt_07.label: Close — why this matters
edt_07.title: A map of life's hidden order
edt_07.editorial_notes: End on the quiet observation that laughter rate is roughly flat across macro topics — all the variation is structural. Leave the reader with a prompt: look at the first 10 minutes of the next special you watch.
